content.title: Denny Hamlin holds off Chase Elliott to win Pennzoil 400 — PHOTOS
content.text: A pit road speeding penalty early in the NASCAR Cup Series Pennzoil 400 on Sunday at Las Vegas Motor Speedway wasn’t going to derail Denny Hamlin from his chances at winning. Especially given what Hamlin has been through since his last win, at the South Point 400 on Oct. 12 at LVMS. Story continues after advertisement Hamlin overcame the penalty, passed teammate Christopher Bell on a restart with 50 laps to go and held off a late charge from Chase Elliott for the victory. “It’s really gratifying,” Hamlin said. “We were really strong here in the fall. It was about eight races ago that we were here. We just took what we had there and refined it and made it better. That was one of the strongest races that I’ve had as a driver in quite some time.” Hamlin started second and led a race-high 134 laps. Elliott finished .504 seconds behind Hamlin after his late charge. William Byron was third, and pole-sitter Christopher Bell was fourth. Hamlin’s win was his 61st in the Cup Series, which breaks a tie for 10th all time on the series wins list with Kevin Harvick. The victory was his third at LVMS. ‘In a great headspace’ The 45-year-old Hamlin has been through a whirlwind since the South Point win. Story continues after advertisement That victory locked him into last year’s Championship 4 race in Phoenix, where Hamlin dominated and was several laps from winning his first title. But a late caution and call to take four tires on a pit stop cost Hamlin his track position, and he lost out on his chance to win the title. After the season, 23XI Racing, the team Hamlin co-owns with NBA legend Michael Jordan, was in court for its antitrust lawsuit against NASCAR in December. Both sides settled after eight days in court that allowed 23XI Racing to keep its charters. Story continues after advertisement Later that month, Hamlin lost his father and his mother was seriously injured in a house fire on Hamlin’s property. Hamlin dedicated his win at Las Vegas in October to his father, who was too ill to attend races last year, in an emotional postrace interview. On Sunday, Hamlin celebrated the win on the frontstretch with his two oldest daughters, who climbed into Hamlin’s car and rode it all the way to victory lane inside the Neon Garage at LVMS. “We worked really hard,” Hamlin said. “The start of the season started a little slow. I probably wasn’t 100 percent focused on the job at hand, but over the last few weeks, we’ve turned the page and things have gotten better. I feel in a great headspace, and it’s gratifying to me being that I’m the oldest guy out there and still can compete.” On being able to celebrate Sunday with his family, Hamlin said: “It’s great. They weren’t here for 60. To have 61, now that they’re able to enjoy it, that was the first time they got to ride in the car after the race, so it’s awesome because I want them to enjoy it like I do.” Story continues after advertisement ‘Take it easy’ Bell was strong early, winning Stage 1. Then Hamlin, from third place, was nabbed for being too fast in pit road while pitting under caution, which sent the No. 11 Joe Gibbs Racing Toyota to the tail end of the field. Hamlin made quick work passing through the field in Stage 2 to finish fifth in the stage. “It was crazy because when I went to the back of the back, the car drove totally different, but I was still able to maneuver and find air when I needed it,” Hamlin said when asked about the advantage of having clean air. “I knew it was crucial on that last restart with 50 to go, get the lead we got (passing) Bell. I could just take it easy, manage my tires and keep the gaps that I need to win.” Gaining ‘momentum’ Hamlin kept fighting his way to the lead. He was battling with Byron just before a caution came out with 57 laps to go for the only accident of the day, a spin involving rookie Connor Zilisch. Bell won the race off pit road for the final pit stops to set up the final restart, but Hamlin powered past his teammate and had just enough to hold off the rest of the field. “We were able to fine-tune (what we had last fall) a little more and let’s exploit what we think was better. I was optimistic,” said Hamlin’s crew chief, Chris Gayle. Story continues after advertisement “It was nice and rewarding,” Gayle added. “I got a little worried about the pit road speeding penalty because you can get trapped in somebody else’s stuff. He did a great job. He buckled down, he was going to make up for it and got through traffic pretty way.” Hamlin jumped eight spots from 12th to fourth in the point standings. He’s 78 points behind series leader Tyler Reddick, who drives for Hamlin’s 23XI Racing. It’s the third top 10 finish of the season for Hamlin, who was coming off a fifth-place run at Phoenix last week. “Momentum means something in this sport, especially for me personally,” Hamlin said. “I’m just waiting on that morning that I wake up and don’t have the skill set that I had before, and things start being slower, and I start not reacting at the same rate I used to before. “But not today.” Contact Alex Wright at awright@reviewjournal.com.
